title: Molten Chocolate Cakes
summary: Individual baked chocolate puddings with a soft, flowing centre, ready in minutes and best served straight from the oven with ice cream.
equipment: 4 metal pudding moulds or ramekins (about 175 ml)
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cubed, plus extra for the moulds
fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
vanilla ice cream (gelatine-free; 4 scoops), to serve

steps.title: Prepare the moulds
steps.text: Butter the pudding moulds thoroughly, then dust with the cocoa powder and tap out the excess. This thorough prep matters because the cakes are delicate and will only turn out cleanly if the moulds are properly coated.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate and butter
steps.text: Melt the butter and chocolate together in a heatproof bowl set over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth, then leave to cool for 5 minutes. Melting them together gently keeps the mixture glossy and stops the chocolate from seizing.

steps.title: Whisk eggs and fold together
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, sugar and salt on high speed for 4-5 minutes until pale and thick. Fold in the cooled chocolate mixture, then fold in the flour just until no streaks remain. Folding the flour in minimally keeps the cakes tender rather than tough, since overworking develops gluten that fights the soft centre.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Divide the batter evenly among the moulds. They can be chilled for up to 24 hours at this point if making ahead; just add 2 minutes to the baking time to allow for the cold start.

steps.title: Bake until set at the edge
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) for at least 20 minutes with a baking tray inside to heat up. Bake the cakes on the hot tray for 9-11 minutes, until the sides are set and firm but the centre is still visibly soft and wobbly when the mould is gently shaken. The very high heat cooks the outside quickly while the centre stays molten, which is the whole point of the dish.

steps.title: Turn out and serve
steps.text: Rest the cakes for 1 minute, run a thin knife around the edge of each mould, then turn them out onto plates. Serve immediately with a scoop of ice cream, before the molten centre has a chance to firm up. Because the centre is deliberately undercooked, it still contains lightly cooked egg, so use eggs from a source you trust and avoid serving this dish to anyone who is pregnant, very young, elderly or has a weakened immune system.

tips: Heat the tray in the oven before the cakes go in - baking straight on a hot tray helps set the outside fast enough to protect the molten centre.
Don't overfold the flour into the batter, or the cakes turn out tough instead of tender around their soft middles.
Watch the bake time closely: even 1-2 minutes too long and the centre sets solid instead of staying molten.
Because the centre stays deliberately soft and contains lightly cooked egg, this dish isn't suitable for pregnant, very young, elderly or immunocompromised diners.
If chilling the filled moulds ahead, remember to add the extra 2 minutes of baking time to account for the cold start.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: These are best baked and eaten immediately, since the molten centre doesn't hold or reheat well. If needed, the filled moulds can be chilled, not frozen, for up to 24 hours before baking.
